title: Ankhorage Project Detector
summary: Detects project languages, frameworks, runtimes, packages, workspaces, and manifests through pure evidence analysis and bounded filesystem inspection.
purpose: Give standalone tools safe, extensible project evidence without executing inspected project code.
responsibilities: Detect overlapping language, framework, runtime, build-tool, and package-manager evidence.
Inspect directory trees with bounded asynchronous read-only filesystem access.
Resolve JavaScript package and workspace membership from package.json workspaces and pnpm YAML.
Expose pure, Node, CLI, and Ankh capability entrypoints with portable result types.
boundaries: Does not execute inspected JavaScript, Gradle, Python, install, or configuration code.
Does not resolve dependency updates, query registries, run migrations, or modify the inspected project.
Does not claim full workspace resolution for ecosystems without an explicit adapter.
audience: Standalone developer tools that need project-shape evidence.
CLI and Ankh hosts inspecting source trees without trusting project code.
useCases: Detect multiple applicable languages and frameworks from supplied evidence.
Inspect a project directory with explicit depth, entry-count, and manifest-byte budgets.
Enumerate files, directories, packages, and JavaScript workspaces without executing the target.
Extend detection through explicitly supplied trusted detector callbacks.

architecture.role: A pure detection core plus a bounded Node filesystem adapter and thin CLI/capability delivery edges.
invariants: Detection evidence is additive and scores are heuristic strengths rather than probabilities.
Filesystem inspection is read-only, bounded, and reports incompleteness instead of granting execution permission.
Symlink targets are never intentionally scanned.
Portable public types are owned and exported by this package.

platforms: Pure JavaScript environments for evidence analysis
security: Inspected project code is never executed; symlink targets are skipped and bounded scans prune dependency and cache directories.
limitations: Non-JavaScript ecosystem manifests are identified but not fully resolved into dependency graphs or workspaces.
